name: Pullman estate (1800 S. Calumet Avenue): the east-west glasshouse range, K13

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the sheet-28 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-28.json, allocation s28-pullman-service-garden) rules the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground present in 1904. Its building date, which the census reads off the 1894 conservatory plate, is T-3165's to read from the pictures themselves.

placement.position_note: The north-west corner, read off the committed sheet 28 raster at pixel (3186, 2447) where the drawn wall lines cross, and carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json; 1.47 m RMS on independent standing houses): local E 1470.61, N -3279.13. The bearing turns the plan onto the sheet's own ruled lines (1.014 degrees off east in that fit), so the building runs square to the lot as drawn.
placement.symbolic_location: 1800 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_1800 (data/street_grid/1904.json): the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground across 18th Street from the house, west side of Calumet Avenue between 18th and 20th Streets; the range running east from the lodge along the lot's south line.

footprint.note: From the corner at the origin, u along the range and v across it (v = -z of the kit's plan, so north on an east-west range and east on a north-south one). The drawn wall lines' centres on the sheet (x 3186-3519, y 2447-2588) at 0.0506 m a pixel: 16.84 by 7.13 m. Its west end is the lodge's east wall; its east end meets the rounded end.

stories.note: The sheet prints '1' on the glasshouse: one storey.

construction.note: Lettered 'GLASS R'F' / 'GLASS ROOF' on the sheet, over the blue wash this copy gives the whole glasshouse ground. The kit stands the glass on a brick plinth.

conservatory.note: The plan is the sheet's (inferred): the range from the lodge's east wall to the line where the narrower rounded end begins. The dashed line the sheet draws across it 2.9 m from the lodge is a partition, not built. Twelve bays, a 2.4 m eave and a 30 degree roof under a ridge ventilator; its west end is the lodge's east wall (abuts end_left); everything else is RECONSTRUCTED from the K13 kit (data/components/prairie_1904/k13_conservatories.json, L-k13-conservatory-kit-2305) and recorded as L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164.

function.note: The 1911 sheet letters the range 'GREEN HO.' with a glass roof ('GLASS R'F' / 'GLASS ROOF'), and the sheet-28 census allocates it to the Pullman estate (s28-pullman-service-garden), on the placement of Beman's conservatory 'across 18th Street from the house (toward Calumet)' in the image research; no deed has been read. The census row is s28-pullman-greenhouse-east ('GREEN HO. GLASS ROOF').

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-3164 (piece 1 of T-1934): Pullman's glasshouse ground across 18th Street, which the district draft left empty because the sheet-28 trace never drew it (T-2335, L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335). Read off sheet 28 by hand at the pixels named in each note, as T-2306 read the house's own bay off sheet 20, because the colour trace cannot separate these ranges: the lodge's pink wash spills diagonally across the east range on this copy. Every size above the plan is the K13 kit's reconstruction (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). T-3165 works the glasshouses to the 1894 plates and the photographs and replaces what they contradict.
